cells.tense: The fair call is being made here, now, and the pen is in your hand for it.
cells.act: take in the yield of what was transformed
cells.ask: Name something a hard change left you — a skill, a person, a clearer line — and hold it as yours. Take a minute with it. Don't tidy the edges off, and don't rush on to the next thing.
cells.core:
When something between people needs weighing, you can hold the whole of it and still land on fair. A feeling doesn't get punished, and a feeling doesn't get the last word either. You let it finish, then you rule, and the ruling lands after rather than over the top of it. That's the good version: the trip keeps its pace and the decisions hold without you hauling them.

It bends when a change you made goes uncounted. You're already moving toward the next thing and the last one's fruit sits untouched. So take in one piece of it — what a hard stretch actually left you. Naming it plainly lets the last thing finish before the next one starts, which is how momentum stays clean instead of running on fumes.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold the whole of it and still call it fair.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed against what's left, and calling it fair
cells.place: on the road between here and where you're headed, with the pace set by the trip

cells.tense: The verdict will be set before the thing it judges has even happened.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Choose one person carrying something heavy. Give them a concrete hand — a ride, a meal, an hour — and see the whole thing through. Then leave it alone and don't grade how it went.
cells.core:
Where you're headed, the calls are getting made before the events. Someone is about to do something, and the judgment is already written; it arrives before the thing has had its hour. That isn't a broken compass — it's the compass running so hard it's reading futures. Fairness at that speed registers as a verdict they didn't see coming.

Put the weight somewhere it can hold. Someone near you has a load, and you have hands. Give one concrete thing — a ride, a meal, an hour — and finish it, without checking whether it landed. Holding up somebody else steadies a compass that's been spinning at the future. The fair call about you comes back when you stop gripping the wheel so tight.
cells.sheetLine: You're ruling on things before they've happened.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed against what's left, and calling it fair

cells.tense: The fair call was yours to make, and it got made a while back, and it sits behind you.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Pick one person stuck on something you already got through. Point them to the single step that moved you, once, plainly. Then stop there and leave the rest to them.
cells.core:
Where the weighing happens, the scale has gone quiet. Something went lopsided and no one set it right, and the person who could have called it fair stepped back. That call was yours, it happened a while back, and it sits behind you now. Momentum is there, but it's pointed backward, and the road ahead is getting paid for in old fuel.

What loosens it: you know a passage someone else is stuck on. You got through something and you know the step that moved you. Point them to it, once, plainly, and stop there. Showing a way you already found tells your own body the road is real, and that you're facing forward again.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's fair and the calling has gone quiet.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed against what's left, and calling it fair
cells.place: on the road between here and where you're headed, with the pace set by the trip

cells.tense: The sense of what's fair is reading true and getting filed under instinct, mood, a gut thing.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Make a list of the pulls on you — people, plans, shoulds. Beside each, write whose it is. No fixing or sorting past that. Just the list and the marks, nothing else.
cells.core:
You can feel what's fair between people, and you keep moving toward what you're headed for, and by your own account the fairness part isn't doing anything. It reads true and gets filed as instinct, or mood, or a gut thing. The course corrections you make for other people get logged as efficiency. The people who benefit from them don't buy the story, and they don't need to.

Most of what pulls at you is borrowed. Put it all in one list and mark whose each thing is. That's the whole act — seeing whose weight you've been carrying and letting the borrowed ones show. The compass doesn't need defending. It needs you to see it's been steering, so the steering gets to be yours.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness you call instinct is steering the whole trip.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed against what's left, and calling it fair
cells.place: on the road between here and where you're headed, with the pace set by the trip

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the Too Much cell can know the person is 'ruling on things before they happen' in Drive specifically — I only have the general over-expressing pattern, so I narrow to what a camera could see: verdicts arriving ahead of events, plans held to before they're due. The reader's likely objection in Balanced: 'I don't feel fair right now, I feel tired' — but the capacity named is the weighing, not the contentment, and the ask doesn't require feeling fair, only that the fruit of a change gets counted. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small concrete act that teaches something even if the read is off. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line about 'your inner compass knowing what's right' — that flatters the reader, so it's kept out.
